title: PDO Database Connection
description: Securely connecting to a MySQL database using PDO.
code:
<?php
$host = '127.0.0.1';
$db   = 'test_db';
$user = 'root';
$pass = '';
$charset = 'utf8mb4';

$dsn = "mysql:host=$host;dbname=$db;charset=$charset";
$options = [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE            => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES   => false,
];

try {
     $pdo = new PDO($dsn, $user, $pass, $options);
} catch (\PDOException $e) {
     throw new \PDOException($e->getMessage(), (int)$e->getCode());
}
explanation_md: PDO (PHP Data Objects) provides a consistent interface for accessing many different databases and encourages secure practices like prepared statements.

title: Password Hashing
description: Securely hashing and verifying passwords.
code:
<?php
// Hashing
$password = 'user_secret_password';
$hash = password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT);

// Verification
if (password_verify($password, $hash)) {
    echo 'Password is valid!';
} else {
    echo 'Invalid password.';
}
explanation_md: Uses PHP's built-in `password_hash` and `password_verify` functions, which implement industry-standard hashing algorithms (currently bcrypt).

title: Simple File Upload
description: Handling a single file upload with basic validation.
code:
<?php
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] == 'POST' && isset($_FILES['my_file'])) {
    $targetDir = "uploads/";
    $targetFile = $targetDir . basename($_FILES["my_file"]["name"]);
    $fileType = strtolower(pathinfo($targetFile, PATHINFO_EXTENSION));

    if ($_FILES["my_file"]["size"] < 500000 && $fileType == "jpg") {
        if (move_uploaded_file($_FILES["my_file"]["tmp_name"], $targetFile)) {
            echo "File uploaded successfully.";
        }
    }
}
explanation_md: Demonstrates the basic process of handling the `$_FILES` superglobal to move a file from a temporary location to a permanent one.

title: Singleton Pattern in PHP
description: Ensuring a class has only one instance.
code:
<?php
class Database {
    private static $instance = null;

    private function __construct() { /* Private constructor */ }

    public static function getInstance() {
        if (self::$instance === null) {
            self::$instance = new self();
        }
        return self::$instance;
    }

    private function __clone() { /* Disable cloning */ }
}
explanation_md: The Singleton pattern restricts the instantiation of a class to one 'single' instance. This is useful for shared resources like database connections.
